project_scope.note: Current canonical website imagery is Salvia-heavy; the lesson explicitly protects against overfitting the whole family to Salvia.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at a node: leaves are usually opposite/decussate and stipules are absent. Then inspect the tubular flower, ovary/style and fruit.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbaceous stems are often quadrangular and foliage often aromatic, but neither character is mandatory.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Corolla commonly bilabiate; stamens commonly 4 or 2; ovary often deeply 4-lobed with a gynobasic style.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Commonly four nutlets inside a persistent calyx, with important exceptions such as drupaceous Callicarpa.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Square stem + opposite leaves is only a clue. The ovary/style/fruit pattern is much stronger.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → exception/tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Use the node as the doorway, but let the flower center and fruit confirm the mint family.

steps.title: 1 · Start at the node
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves at a node; successive pairs often rotate 90° (decussate).
steps.why_it_matters: This is a fast first-pass cue shared by many local mints.

steps.title: 2 · Check the flower tube
steps.look_for: A fused tubular corolla with upper and lower lips.
steps.why_it_matters: Pairs the vegetative node cue with a common reproductive family pattern.

steps.title: 3 · Notice the Salvia exception
steps.look_for: Only two fertile stamens and the specialized connective/lever system.
steps.why_it_matters: Stops the learner from memorizing 'mint = four stamens.'

steps.title: 4 · Confirm fruit architecture
steps.look_for: A deeply 4-lobed superior ovary and later four nutlets within a persistent calyx.
steps.why_it_matters: This is stronger than stem shape for separating Lamiaceae from lookalikes.

comparisons.title: Lamiaceae vs Verbenaceae
comparisons.rule: Do not use square stems alone. The common mint pattern has a deeply 4-lobed ovary and often a gynobasic style with four nutlets; Verbenaceae commonly differs in style/ovary and fruit architecture.

comparisons.title: Lamiaceae vs Rubiaceae
comparisons.rule: Rubiaceae has interpetiolar stipules and an inferior ovary; Lamiaceae lacks stipules and has a superior ovary.

visual_lesson.caveat: Salvia is an excellent local teaching genus, but Lamiaceae also includes woody, radial-flowered and drupaceous-fruited exceptions.
